task: Meta-analysis of metabolic biomarkers (Glucose, BMI, BloodPressure) vs chronic diseases (Diabetes, Stroke, HeartDisease) across 3 healthcare datasets

data_inputs.role: Diabetes outcome; continuous Glucose / BloodPressure(diastolic) / BMI
Stroke and HeartDisease outcomes; continuous avg_glucose_level / bmi (BP only binary -> unusable)
HeartDisease outcome (num>0); continuous trestbps (systolic BP) with a site column 'dataset' enabling 4 sub-studies

analysis_unit.definition: One row of the final results = one (condition, biomarker) association. 8 associations in total (3 conditions x 3 biomarkers, minus Stroke-BloodPressure which has no continuous BP).
analysis_unit.rationale: No (biomarker, disease) pair is measured in more than one dataset, except BloodPressure-HeartDisease which can be split into 4 UCI site sub-studies; therefore only that pair supports a true inverse-variance weighted pooling, all others are single-study meta-analyses of one estimate.

associations.note: DIASTOLIC BP (mmHg) - never pooled with systolic trestbps
UCI heart dataset has only the binary 'fbs' flag -> must NOT be substituted
UCI heart dataset has no BMI column

associations.study_unit: per site, groupby 'dataset' -> 4 sub-studies (Cleveland, Hungary, Switzerland, VA Long Beach)
associations.note: SYSTOLIC resting BP. Only multi-study pair -> IVW fixed-effect meta-analysis.

cleaning_rules.general: All cleaning is PER-ASSOCIATION (pairwise deletion): drop rows with missing biomarker AND missing outcome only within the current pair; never listwise-delete across biomarkers.
Healthcare-Diabetes.csv: Replace physiologically impossible 0 with NaN in Glucose, BloodPressure, BMI (0 = missing-code, not a real measurement).
Do not touch SkinThickness/Insulin (unused). Keep rows with valid biomarker; no upper-bound trimming.
healthcare-dataset-stroke-data.csv: bmi = pd.to_numeric(bmi, errors='coerce') to convert the 201 literal 'N/A' strings to NaN.

Keep implausible extremes (bmi>60: 13, bmi<12: 3, age<1: 43) in the primary analysis; flag them as sensitivity-only items and report a sensitivity re-run excluding bmi>60 and age<1, but DO NOT silently drop in the primary results.
heart_disease_uci.csv: trestbps = pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); replace 0 with NaN (59 nulls + 1 zero).
Site = 'dataset' column; site sub-studies formed by groupby('dataset').
Drop site sub-study if n_cases < 5 or n_controls < 5 (guard; Switzerland has 8 controls so it is retained but heavily down-weighted by IVW).

effect_size.direction_convention: d = (mean_cases - mean_controls) / pooled_sd; positive d = biomarker HIGHER in diseased group. All 8 pairs expected positive.
guards: If pooled_sd == 0 or n1<2 or n0<2 -> drop that study and log it (should not happen).
effect_size.optional_sensitivity: Also record Hedges' g = d * (1 - 3/(4*(n1+n0)-9)); report only as sensitivity, not in the deliverable columns.

meta_analysis.single_study_pairs: With one study the formulas collapse to meta_effect_size = d_1, se = se_d_1; the p-value is still computed from the z-score with a two-tailed normal test (N(0,1)), NOT a t-distribution — per task specification.
meta_analysis.multi_study_pair_HDF_BP: Pool the 4 UCI site-level d_i with the weights above (fixed effect). Expected: all sites positive d, small heterogeneity; optionally report I^2/Q as a note but fixed-effect estimate is the deliverable.
heterogeneity_optional: Report in a supplementary key only; do not switch to random effects.
meta_analysis.p_value_underflow: Compute in float64; if p underflows to exactly 0, floor it at 1e-300 before FDR so that -log10() and BH remain finite (the +1e-10 in the score already prevents log(0)).

multiple_testing.family: All 8 (condition, biomarker) associations from the primary analysis, corrected together as a single family.
procedure: Order the 8 raw p-values ascending: p_(1) <= ... <= p_(m), m = 8.
Enforce monotonicity from the largest i down: q_(i) = min(q_(i), q_(i-1)) applied as cumulative minimum from the top.
Cap at 1.0; map back to the original association order.
multiple_testing.note: Apply BH on unrounded p-values; only round the reported fdr_corrected_p to 6 dp afterwards.

clinical_significance.computation_detail: Use UNROUNDED |meta_effect_size| and UNROUNDED fdr_corrected_p for the score; only the final score-based ranking is reported.
clinical_significance.rank: clinical_significance_rank = 1 for the largest score, ascending to N=8 (rank 1 = most clinically significant).

confidence_classification.evaluation_detail: Evaluate with UNROUNDED fdr_corrected_p and UNROUNDED |meta_effect_size|; the thresholds are strict inequalities. Apply 'high' check first, then 'medium', else 'low'.

primary.empty_value_policy: No blank cells; every association row must be emitted even if labelled 'low'.

fields: method notes: fixed-effect IVW, two-tailed normal p, BH-FDR over 8 tests, unrounded values used for scoring/classification

outputs.optional_supplementary: meta_analysis_per_study_effects.csv with one row per (association, study/site) holding n_cases, n_controls, mean/sd per group, d, se, weight — for auditability. Recommended but not required.

validation_checkpoints.row_count: meta_analysis_results.csv must have exactly 8 data rows.
validation_checkpoints.direction: All 8 meta_effect_size values must be > 0 (biomarker higher in cases).
validation_checkpoints.reproduce_profile_descriptives: Group n / mean / sd must match data_profile.json feasibility_matrix within tolerance 1e-3 (e.g. DIA_GLU: n_cases 944 mean 142.6801 sd 29.3355; n_controls 1806 mean 111.031 sd 25.1496).
validation_checkpoints.magnitude_expectation: Glucose-Diabetes ~1.2 (largest); Glucose-Stroke and Glucose-HeartDisease ~0.6-0.7; BloodPressure-HeartDisease ~0.25 (smallest). Large deviations (>30%) indicate a wrong group definition or unit mix-up.
validation_checkpoints.fdr_sanity: fdr_corrected_p >= meta_p_value for every row; min fdr_corrected_p == min p * 8/rank_min (BH with i=1 gives 8*p_min unless capped).
validation_checkpoints.rank_sanity: clinical_significance_rank is a permutation of 1..8 with no duplicates or gaps.
validation_checkpoints.confidence_sanity: Every 'high' row satisfies p_fdr<0.01 and |d|>0.5 on unrounded values; recompute from the reported (unrounded) internals if possible.

negative_constraints: Do NOT use binary indicators as biomarker substitutes: stroke 'hypertension' -> not BloodPressure; UCI 'fbs' -> not Glucose.
Do NOT pool BloodPressure across datasets/diseases (diastolic Pima vs systolic UCI are different units/constructs); the BP-Diabetes and BP-HeartDisease estimates stay separate.
Do NOT pool Glucose across diseases (fasting Pima vs avg_glucose_level stroke cohort have different sampling); pairs stay separate.
Do NOT add Cholesterol/other biomarkers; only Glucose, BMI, BloodPressure.
Do NOT include a Stroke-BloodPressure row (no continuous BP available).
Do NOT re-derive or overwrite data_profile.json.
Do NOT use imputation or listwise deletion across biomarkers.
risks_and_limitations: 7 of 8 associations are single-study, so 'meta-analysis' reduces to one estimate; pooled p-values reflect within-study precision only (no between-study generalisation).
The only true pooling (BP-HeartDisease) rests on 4 UCI sites with very different case/control ratios (Switzerland 113 vs 8); IVW down-weights it but site heterogeneity limits inference.
BloodPressure mixes diastolic (Diabetes pair) and systolic (HeartDisease pair) constructs -> results are not comparable across the two BP rows.
Observational data: association, not causation; no adjustment for age/sex/medication confounding.
Implausible BMI extremes and pediatric rows retained in the primary analysis (sensitivity analysis recommended).
Cohen's d with strongly unequal group sizes (e.g. Stroke 249 vs 4861) is dominated by control-group SD; small absolute mean differences can still yield modest d.
execution_steps_for_downstream_node: 1. Load the three CSVs (pandas); apply cleaning_rules per file.
2. Build the 8 association datasets per 'associations'; for HDF_BP split heart_disease_uci by 'dataset' into 4 site studies.
3. For each association compute per-study n1,m1,s1,n0,m0,s0 -> d, var_d, se_d (unrounded).
4. Pool with IVW (single-study associations pass through unchanged); compute z and two-tailed normal p.
5. Apply BH-FDR across the 8 raw p-values.
6. Compute score = |meta_d| * (-log10(p_fdr + 1e-10)), assign ranks with tie-breakers, assign confidence levels (all on unrounded values).
7. Round for reporting (4 dp effect, 6 dp p-values), sort by rank, write meta_analysis_results.csv.
9. Run validation_checkpoints; if any fails, fix before finishing.
